articles.standfirst: David Ferrer presenta en Madrid a sus cinco jugadores, adelantados por MARCA, de cara a la 'Final a 8'
articles.summary: David Ferrer presenta en Madrid a sus cinco jugadores, adelantados por MARCA, de cara a la 'Final a 8'
articles.body: David Ferrer, junto al presidente de la Federación Española de Tenis, Miguel Díaz Román, ha hecho oficial este lunes en Madrid la lista del equipo español de cara a la Final a 8 de la Copa Davis de Bolonia (24 al 29 de noviembre). Tal y como adelantó MARCA, Carlos Alcaraz, Rafa Jódar, Alejandro Davidovich, Marcel Granollers y Pedro Martínez, estos dos últimos para el dobles, son los elegidos por el capitán. Atendiendo el ranking ATP, será el equipo más potente sobre las pistas de Bolonia. Tres jugadores entre los 15 primeros de la clasificación alaban esta condición. “Yo espero que ganando la Davis en un mes, te quedes David”, dijo Miguel Díaz Román. La novedad ha estado en la inclusión final de Alejandro Davidovich. Aunque ha hecho méritos para ello. El malagueño ha levantado tres títulos esta temporada: Mallorca, Chengdú y Shanghai, este último de categoría 1000. El nuevo número 13 del mundo se ha convertido en el único tenista español en hacerse con el certamen chino. España arrancará el camino hacia la séptima ensaladera ante Austria el 26 de noviembre, que tiene a Jurij Rodionov (137 del mundo) como su mejor baza.

articles.title: Alcaraz y Zverev promocionan el torneo de Viena desde la Ópera
articles.standfirst: Los dos primeros favoritos han posado en el edificio neorrenacentista, uno de los símbolos de la capital austriaca
articles.summary: Los dos primeros favoritos han posado en el edificio neorrenacentista, uno de los símbolos de la capital austriaca
articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz y Alexander Zverev vuelven a encontrarse en el cuadro de un torneo después de haberlo hecho en el Masters 1000 de Shanghái. No hubo allí duelo entre ambos en la pista porque la final la protagonizaron Rafa Jódar y Alejandro Davidovich, con victoria de este último. Antes de iniciar este martes su participación en el torneo de categoría 500, Alcaraz y Zverev se juntaron la tarde del domingo para visitar la Ópera Estatal de Viena. Incluso han llegado a pelotear en las escaleras. El edificio neorrenacentista, construido entre 1861 y 1869, es uno de los símbolos de la capital austriaca. El Marx Halle, donde se disputa la competición de tenis, está situado a algo más de cuatro kilómetros. El torneo podría ser recordado toda la vida en el caso de Zverev. Y es que el alemán saldrá el próximo lunes 2 de noviembre como primero del ranking ATP en caso de alcanzar los cuartos.

articles.title: El Six Kings Slam anuncia la vuelta de Sinner
articles.standfirst: El italiano se ha sometido a un tratamiento conservador en la rodilla derecha y está a la espera de los resultados
articles.summary: El italiano se ha sometido a un tratamiento conservador en la rodilla derecha y está a la espera de los resultados
articles.body: El Six Kings Slam, tras verse obligado a retrasar sus fechas (27 al 30 de diciembre) por los recientes ataques en Riad, ha anunciado la vuelta de Jannik Sinner a su competición. Previamente, debido a su reciente baja para lo que resta de 2026, el torneo saudí había encontrado su sustituto en el joven Learner Tien, pero tras el inesperado movimiento en el calendario, han optado por volver a contar con la participación momentánea del italiano. Aunque todo está sujeto a como evolucione el tratamiento al que se está sometiendo el transalpino en su rodilla derecha. Debido a que el método conservador que llevó a cabo tras Wimbledon no surgió efecto, Sinner, el 6 de octubre, anunció su baja definitiva para 2026: "Hemos decidido con los médicos realizar un tratamiento en la rodilla por lo que la temporada 2026 se ha acabado oficialmente para mí... tengo que pensar en mi carrera a largo plazo", alegó el campeón de cinco grandes. Sin todavía conocer como responderá el de San Cándido a la recuperación, la organización del Six Kings Slam ha decidido volver a incluirle en sus planes junto a Carlos Alcaraz, Alexander Zverev, Novak Djokovic, Taylor Fritz y Alex de Miñaur. Y el propio tenista ha decidido compartir el anuncio en su cuenta de Instagram.

articles.title: ATP doubles proposals: Players and legends sign open letter to prevent cuts
articles.summary: More than 150 doubles players - including Wimbledon champions and tennis legends - urge the ATP to rethink "drastic" cuts which they believe could kill the format.
articles.body:
More than 150 men's doubles players - including British world number one Henry Patten and the legendary Bryan brothers - have urged the ATP Tour to rethink "drastic" changes which they believe could kill the format.

In a show of collective action, the players have written an open letter to the men's governing body as they fight proposals which would cut draw sizes and reduce prize money from 2028.

"We're at risk of losing a discipline of tennis which is historic - but has a big future," Dutch player Sem Verbeek, one of the architects of the letter, told BBC Sport.

"These proposals would destroy careers, livelihoods and dreams."

The ATP proposed halving the doubles draws at its flagship Masters 1000 events to 16 teams, with smaller tournaments reduced to eight teams.

The percentage of prize money devoted to doubles could fall from 20% to 10% - with the difference redistributed to singles players.

'You're taking our jobs' - doubles players angry at proposed cuts

On Monday, a group of 137 current players, 28 legends and 20 national federations signed a letter which they hope will pressure the ATP into rethinking the proposals.

The tour's board - comprised of chairman Andrea Gaudenzi, four tournament representatives and four player representatives - will vote on the plans at next month's ATP Finals in Turin.

The doubles reform is part of a wider review by the ATP, which it says is designed to "strengthen" the tour from 2028.

The ATP aims to create "a more sustainable long-term model", insisting it wants to "maintain the important role" of doubles.

"Commercial success matters. Fairness, player welfare and the long-term health of tennis matter just as much," the players' letter says.

"Let us grow tennis together, without leaving doubles players behind."

The proposals provoked an angry response from the men's doubles cohort when they were revealed in July.

British pair Lloyd Glasspool and Julian Cash, who won Wimbledon in 2025 and became world number ones, accused the ATP of trying to "kill part of the sport".

Others within tennis believe reform is needed. They suggest a 20% share of the prize money for doubles is disproportionate to the interest shown by fans.

The doubles players argue the ATP should do more to promote their discipline and attract greater audiences, pointing out it is the format played by most club members and therefore more relatable.

The ATP says the proposals are based on data-led analysis centred on costs, revenue and viewership.

With fewer singles players now competing in doubles, it believes the current size of the standalone doubles events puts severe strain on tournaments.

"We support progress. We also understand the need to grow the sport, strengthen tournaments and increase commercial value," the players' letter says.

"Still, the proposed reforms go much too far."

Reigning Wimbledon champion Patten recently told BBC Sport the players were facing "an uphill battle", but remained "optimistic" the tour would consider counter-proposals. Since Wimbledon there have been several meetings between both sides, including recently at the Shanghai Masters.

The players still believe there is little appetite for negotiation from the ATP. But ATP sources insist a compromise is likely to be found.

Mike and Bob Bryan - the identical twins considered the greatest doubles pair of all-time - said they would support the group considering legal action to protect their discipline.

In 2005, the American brothers led players in a lawsuit against the ATP, when it planned radical changes to doubles.

"The tour's in the healthiest financial state it's ever been - in our opinion it should be creating more opportunities," Bob Bryan told BBC Sport in an interview at Wimbledon in July.

Mike Bryan added: "These proposed changes are anti-competitive. That's the stance we had to take in 2005. We still believe in doubles and we believe in the players fighting for this."

articles.title: Rafael Nadal Will Play in Tennis Exhibition in Las Vegas, 1st U.S. Event Since 2024 Retirement
articles.summary: Rafael Nadal is back. For an exhibition.
articles.body:
Rafael Nadal is back. For an exhibition.

The tennis legend will participate in February's "MGM Slam presented by Capital One" at T-Mobile Arena, per the Associated Press , his first return to the court since he retired in Nov. 2024.

"I remember how impressive it was to feel the energy of a full arena in a city like Las Vegas," Nadal said. "Now I return in a different stage of my life, without the pressure of the tour but with the same passion for this sport. I have always loved competing, and even if my professional career is finished, that feeling never really goes away."

The 40-year-old is one of the most decorated players in history, with 92 singles titles on the ATP Tour, 22 Grand Slam titles—including a record 14 triumphs at the French Open—and two gold medals.

articles.title: Jacob Fearnley retires hurt against Arthur Fery at Vienna Open as Harriet Dart extends winning run
articles.summary: Arthur Fery is into the second round of the Vienna Open after fellow Brit Jacob Fearnley retired with an injury in the first set; Harriet Dart has won her third successive match at the Guangzhou Open; watch WTA and ATP Tours live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
Fearnley was broken by Fery in just his second service game, with the British No 1 winning the next two games on the bounce and looking set to consign his opponent to a comprehensive first-set loss.

Fearnley, though, then put a stop to the contest, shaking the umpire's hand and retiring with an unspecified injury, allowing Fery safe passage to the next stage of the competition.

Fery will face the winner of No 6 seed Francis Tiafoe and Lorenzo Musetti - the latter of whom he lost against in straight sets at the US Open - in the second round.

Dart extends winning run in Guangzhou Open

Harriet Dart maintained her winning form at the Guangzhou Open in China as she beat Russian qualifier Tatiana Prozorova 6-4 2-6 6-2 to reach the second round.

Dart, who also came through two qualifiers, will next face Uzbekistan's Polina Kudermetova or Indonesia's Janice Tjen in the last 16 after winning a see-saw battle against world number 123 Prozorova.

Both players struggled to hold serve, but the British number five broke three times in the decider to open up a 5-2 lead and served out to seal victory in two hours and 15 minutes.

British teenager Mika Stojsavljevic slipped to a heavy first-round defeat at the Toray Pan Pacific Open in Tokyo, losing 6-1 6-2 to Filipino world number 19 Alexandra Eala in one hour and 15 minutes.

Stojsavljevic, 17, who won the girls' US Open singles title at the 2024 US Open, was broken twice in both sets by the world number 19 after being given a wildcard into the WTA 500 tournament.

articles.title: Every player who beat Rafael Nadal at the Swiss Indoors in Basel as he never won the title
articles.summary: Rafael Nadal never got his hands on the title at the Swiss Indoors in Basel. The Swiss Indoors is one of the most prestigious tournaments...
articles.body:
Rafael Nadal never got his hands on the title at the Swiss Indoors in Basel.

The Swiss Indoors is one of the most prestigious tournaments on the ATP calendar, and this year it will be holding the 55th edition of the event, featuring the likes of Novak Djokovic , Ben Shelton , Arthur Fils and Rafael Jodar .

Djokovic is a former champion at the Swiss Indoors tournament, alongside a number of other legendary names including Roger Federer , Bjorn Borg , Pete Sampras and John McEnroe .

However, the honour roll does not include Nadal , who was unable to win the title in Basel in any of his four appearances at the tournament.

Rafael Nadal did not win the title in any of his four appearances at the Swiss Indoors

The Swiss Indoors is now held on indoor hard courts, but when Nadal made his debut at the tournament in 2003 it was held on indoor carpet, which is no longer used for ATP events.

Nadal was just 17 years old at the time, and in the first round was drawn to face his compatriot Feliciano Lopez , who he had never played before. This was just Nadal's 10th ATP Tour event, and although he won the first set, he was ultimately beaten 3-6, 6-3, 7-6(4).

The Mallorcan returned to Basel a year later, but Nadal was unable to win a match at the tournament once again, as this time he was beaten by Rainer Schüttler in straight sets.

Nadal did not return to the Swiss Indoors until 10 years later, when the tournament was now on indoor hard courts. Nadal won his first two matches at the tournament after obtaining emphatic wins over Simone Bolelli and Pierre-Hugues Herbert by dropping just six games in two matches. Despite his dominant start to the tournament, Nadal was stunned in the quarter-finals by Borna Coric.

The closest Nadal would come to winning the Swiss Indoors was in 2015, when he beat the likes of Grigor Dimitrov , Marin Cilic and Richard Gasquet en route to the final. In this final he would play his great rival Federer, who has won the most titles at the Swiss Indoors in history.

Nadal lost the first set of this final, but fought back to level the match at one set apiece, before Federer took control of the final to win 6-3, 5-7, 6-3.

Year Rafael Nadal played at the Swiss Indoors

What Rafael Nadal said after losing to Roger Federer in the 2015 Basel final

The 2015 Swiss Indoors final was the last time Nadal would ever compete in Basel, but he appeared to be taking the positives from his defeat to Federer.

"The match wasn't far away from me," said Nadal. "He played well and I played well too. The match was very close to win, but I think he served very well in the third.

"I want to congratulate him for the victory and I had a lot of quality things in my game and mental side to take away from the week."

Although Nadal was never able to win the title at the Swiss Indoors, he did win one title on indoor hard courts in his career. This came when the Madrid Open was held on indoor hard courts, with Nadal winning the title in 2005.

However, one of the biggest titles missing from Nadal's collection is also held on indoor hard courts at the ATP Finals , where he twice lost in the final.
